On 2026-10-20 Kenneth looked at a live chat ("Affirmative Response Without Context", project arrow_headband)
where he answered "yes" to switching to the Bambu Lab A1 and the thread grew by 17 Chat/Tool Activity
cards (12 read-only lookups, 5 edits), 17 empty assistant bubbles (one per model response that only called
tools), 8 change rows, then the reply: about three screens for one word. He asked for a new UX.

What I found before proposing:
- The approved print-timeline board on the canvas draws an Agent turn as prose + one summary line
  ("Laid flat · 5 walls · 35% gyroid · +3⌄"); no per-call cards anywhere in the design. The Chat/System
  Line component is specified as "quiet one-line record of ... background agent work".
- The Tool Activity card was designed for approvals (Pending / Approve / Reject); approvals were removed
  2026-10-07 ([[tool-call-approval-removed]]), so the card has no question left to ask.
- Structural cause of the splitting: MessageList groups activities under the assistant message that
  carries their correlationId, and every tool-only response is its own empty message, so one turn becomes
  17 groups and the change rows cannot merge (groupChanges only merges within a block). All 17 messages
  carry inReplyTo m-3, so grouping by turn needs no saved-data change.

The proposal (board "agent-turn-activity · proposal", page Agent UI, x 9209 y 3030, 986×3213; builder
`figma-mirror/tools/composer/build_turn_activity_board.py` reading `turn_yes.json` pulled from the saved
chat): (1) while working, one Chat/System Line under the person's message with the running action's
title + Stop; (2) finished, the same line reads "{n} actions ⌄", the reply lands under it, the turn's
changes follow as one merged block (printer_setup = one row with process and filament in the meta;
3 placements = "3 steps merged"); (3) opened, one line per action, edits in text/primary, lookups in
text/secondary, failures in status/danger with the message. Measured work (slice) keeps its progress card.

Kenneth's three refinements (2026-10-20, same day): no Stop link on the line, the composer's Stop is the
one way to interrupt (it already sends stop_generation; handle_stop cancels the model stream, fires the
turn boundary, and lets a native tool already running finish); the line shows elapsed time, ticking and
shimmering while working, "Worked for 44s · 17 actions" when done (ChatGPT draws "Worked for 1m 9s >",
Claude.ai "Read memory, searched past chats, searched the web >", both opening into a row list); and no
restore point during a turn. Mid-turn versions come from ProjectAutosave's 2-s probe (capture whenever the
model changed and 1.5 s passed), so the fix is a busy predicate wired from ShellController plus a capture
at the existing turn-boundary callback. Board republished with these.

Implemented 2026-10-20 (uncommitted on jusprin-newui, Kenneth chose "plain lines first"): page side
`AgentUI/src/components/TurnActivity.tsx` + `turnsOf` in MessageList (project chat only; printer panel keeps
cards), preset-run merge in ChangeRows (host now sets WorkspaceEdit.location = printer|filament|process),
`createdAt` on WireMessage (host stamps in-memory messages at every append_message call site), token
`component.turnActivity.shimmerMs` = 1600 emitted as `--turn-activity-shimmer-duration`. Host side: the real
source of mid-turn versions was `ShellController`'s tool version callbacks (pin_current before every mutating
call, save_now after), not the autosave probe; now the first edit of a model turn pins once, later edits reuse
it (`m_turn_before_version`), `record_agent_operation(..., save=false)` links only the before-version, the
turn boundary's checkpoint saves the end state, and `ProjectAutosave::set_capture_hold` keeps the probe from
saving the model while `AgentHost::busy()`. Tests: vitest 553 green, agent_bridge_tests 381 green.
Verified live 2026-10-20 (Kenneth approved one turn, Haiku 5.5): line ticked 'Working on it… · 2s/5s/10s', settled to 'Worked for 9s · 3 actions', two object_place calls shared one before-version with after='' and the turn made exactly one new version (changeSeq = its last change). Driving trap: synthesized clicks never focus the WKWebView composer; Tab into the page from the native canvas, then click the field; stray keys hit canvas shortcuts (a slice started).

**How to apply:** every string on a proposal board must come from the saved chat or a named rule
([[mockup-strings-from-real-output]]). Kenneth has not decided yet; check the chat before implementing.
Side findings reported with it: the chat title generator was fed only "yes"; the reply's numbered options
are not chips because the model did not end with "Choices: a | b"; printer_setup_preview said Textured
Cool Plate but printer_setup applied Smooth High Temp Plate.

**2026-10-20 later:** Kenneth read the trailing-edge down/up chevron as wrong. Convention is split (trailing edge: down closed / up open, as Bootstrap and Primer; next to the words: right closed / down open, as ChatGPT, Claude and Apple disclosure). The line now puts the chevron right after the words, right/down. The running glyph (rotate-cw) spins via `component.turnActivity.spinMs` = 1000; a still arrow read as nothing happening.

**Design artifacts updated 2026-10-20:** DS v32 has `ChatTurnActivity` (coded, card, README, tokens
`component-turnActivity-shimmerMs/spinMs`); canvas v40 has the review board
`review-chat-turn-activity-light-dark` (component-review page, x 0 y 564), the turn line in the five
print-timeline boards under User turn 1 and 3 (heights 1500→1580), the proposal board redrawn with the inline
right/down chevron. WebKit centres a flex button's content: `.turn-activity-line` needs
`justify-content: flex-start` (Chrome previews hid it).

Kenneth's charge (2026-10-17) for the project chat's prompt: "the standing prompt carries principles, and everything situational arrives at the moment it applies, from the app, not from the model's memory of a checklist." He judged the 2026-10-15 sectioned prompt (nine-sentence Preparing procedure, print-issue and repeated-request bullets) as not meeting it, and said I underperformed by not looking at the big picture.

**The test for a sentence:** it stays in the standing prompt only if it is true and useful on every turn (a question with no model, a troubleshooting request, a print request alike). Otherwise it goes to the channel that fires when its situation arises: an app note built at request time (last item, never stored, same bytes for the same state), a tool's result (what is now in place and what is still unchecked), a tool's description (a rule about one tool), or the message itself (button sentences, `<workspace>`/`<print_issue>` blocks, the plate picture on file open). A sentence that restates what code enforces is deleted.

**Why:** published practice (Anthropic skills' progressive disclosure, Replit decision-time guidance, Pydantic system reminders, Anthropic tools guide) and our own audit: rule lists fade and lose to the model's priors; four prompt sentences were an agent's precautions or restatements, never observed; the repeated-request line was Codex's own caution on 2026-10-12 and its test was derived from the sentence.

**Form (Kenneth, 2026-10-17, revised later that day):** two kinds of skill, one loader, all `SKILL.md` on the page. An event skill has a `trigger` and the app injects it for the one request where the event happened; the model never chooses it. A discretionary skill has a `description` and the model may read it with the ported `skill_read` (consistent with Claude Code / Agent Skills; common skills may later be offered this way). Event skills never depend on the model choosing; the suspended skills branches (`feature/project-skills-routing`, 2d62184e37 README) failed on model routing and on content that repeated general knowledge, not on the container. Word-only situations get no skill until a transcript shows a gap.

**Groups (Kenneth, 2026-10-17), one chip each, in order:** (1) a model is opened or imported (port the loader and skill_read, migrate the file-open text, fire on tool imports too; project_open by the model interrupts the turn, collects the load report with the existing collector and hands it to the new chat through the file-note path; the skill text adds the preset check and asks whether the AI should look at the model instead of attaching a picture); (2) slicing finished unsuccessfully (refusal reason into the project summary, event-driven slice wait); (3) other OrcaSlicer issues incl. the Explain/Fix canvas buttons; (4) project setup changed after a purpose was recorded. No skill for failed/not-run calls (JusPrin's own words). Prompt shrink is the last step. Tracker table in core-prompt-critique.md, "Skills by event".

**How to apply:** when asked for a prompt rule, first ask which channel the situation belongs to; add a standing sentence only when a measured failure shows the model lacks the principle. The bridging sentence that makes state-delivered guidance work is "When a result or an app note names something unchecked, check it before moving on." The plan and disposition table live in the untracked `core-prompt-critique.md` ("Restructure plan", 2026-10-17), as a proposal: Kenneth wants plans presented and decided, not assumed. On 2026-10-17 he had my fast-forward merge of the state-guidance branch undone for that reason (reset, never revert: a revert would litter the log). Related: [[rule-lives-next-to-what-it-governs]], [[project-prompt-sections]], [[tool-call-approval-removed]].

Rebased onto 87b3c50474 (plate type in the workspace block, which also carries the harness.conf version-check fix) and fast-forwarded into local jusprin-newui: commits 0afbb7ad42, 803f1dd0c5, 8a3db9052d, ce11a1087e; older hashes in this note no longer exist on a branch.

metadata:

---

A rule lives once, as close as possible to the thing it governs: a rule about one tool lives in that tool's description; a rule about the conversation (when to act, when to ask, record intent before preparing, reply language) lives in the prompt.

**Why:** the 2026-10-14 handoff turned "one home per rule" into "the prompt is the home". Applied in 2595f0556c, that stripped one-tool rules (skipped_confirmation settling, export slice check, project_open's message handling, intent_update's "do not infer") out of descriptions, which every caller sees — project, printer and filament chats and MCP clients — and left the other chats and MCP with nothing. The old reason for prompt-side policy, tool deferral hiding descriptions, is gone. Kenneth endorsed the correction on 2026-10-15.

**How to apply:** ask "who needs this rule?" A rule about one tool's arguments or output goes in its description even if it says "ask" or "explain". Check the host's per-turn lines before calling them a rule's home: the "file-load reports are source data" developer line exists only for files the person opened, not for project_open called by the model or for MCP. Also: asking the person when the answer is theirs (which printer they own, which project to continue) is wanted and important; the 2026-10-07 removal was of approval gates on tool calls, not of asking. Related: [[tool-call-approval-removed]], [[project-prompt-sections]], [[orca-edit-questions-forwarded]].

########## ask-decisions-in-full.md
---
name: ask-decisions-in-full
description: When a decision is Kenneth's, state it with complete information (what, why it is his, the options, the consequence of each, my recommendation); never a shorthand like "the go to catch the main checkout up" or "the three harness decisions". Asked 2026-10-14 after two such shorthands.
metadata:

---

On 2026-10-14 I ended a reply with "two things are waiting on you: the go to catch the main checkout up with the rewritten branch, and the three harness decisions from the critique report." Kenneth could not tell whether the first was a decision he had to make, and said the second left him guessing what the decisions were. He asked that this be recorded as a standing rule.

**Why:** a phrase that only makes sense with my working context reads as jargon to him, and a decision he cannot understand is a decision he cannot make. He had no earlier rule about this in CLAUDE.md or memory; the nearest is [[write-like-a-person]].

**How to apply:** every time I need Kenneth to decide something, write it out in full, in its own paragraph or bullet: what the decision is, why it is his and not mine, the options with what each one does and costs, and which one I recommend. Never refer to a decision by a label, a count, or a report it lives in. Check the last paragraph of every reply for this before sending. Related: [[write-like-a-person]], [[report-outcomes-not-obstacles]].

**Added 2026-10-18:** a decision for Kenneth is phrased as a question that ends with "?". He pointed out that three of four "decisions" I listed were statements ("The bed-temperature warning. Tell the model about it, or keep matching..."), and only the one that read as a question was answerable. Each item: the question with "?", the options with consequences, then my recommendation.

**Added 2026-10-19:** a third repeat. I ended a status report with five one-line "still open" items ("Output limit. The Anthropic profile sets 16,000 tokens... One number in the profile."). Kenneth: "I can understand none of these questions since you did not provide the information and the contacts I needed to answer them." A short status recap is not the place for decisions; each needs its own paragraph with the mechanism explained (what the number does, what happens at the limit, what it costs), not just the knob's name. Also check whether an item is a decision at all: one of the five (minProperties in strict mode) had no user-facing effect and should not have been listed.

########## write-like-a-person.md
---
name: write-like-a-person
description: Kenneth finds clipped, label-style bullets ("One home per kind of thing. Standing policy in X, facts in Y.") strange and asked twice on 2026-10-14 to "talk like a human"; write full plain sentences as to a colleague.
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

On 2026-10-14 Kenneth replied to two bullets in a prompt critique ("Mechanics live in the harness, not the prompt. Read-only tools on an explain turn, argument validation, …" and "One home per kind of thing. Standing policy in instructions, facts in a tagged context block, …") with "I don't know why you talk this way. Really strange. Can you talk like a human?"

**Why:** compressed noun-phrase bullets and slogans read as jargon; he wants to be told things the way a colleague would say them out loud, with the concrete case first and the general point after.

**How to apply:** write full sentences with a subject and a verb. Say the concrete thing ("the app currently pastes the project JSON into your message right after what you typed") before any principle. No label-colon fragments, no aphorisms, no abstract nouns standing in for an explanation. When a point needs a technical term, say what it means in the same sentence. Related: [[report-outcomes-not-obstacles]], [[investigation-report-four-part-frame]].

222	
223	Kenneth's charge (2026-10-17) for the project chat's prompt: "the standing prompt carries principles, and everything situational arrives at the moment it applies, from the app, not from the model's memory of a checklist." He judged the 2026-10-15 sectioned prompt (nine-sentence Preparing procedure, print-issue and repeated-request bullets) as not meeting it, and said I underperformed by not looking at the big picture.
224	
225	**The test for a sentence:** it stays in the standing prompt only if it is true and useful on every turn (a question with no model, a troubleshooting request, a print request alike). Otherwise it goes to the channel that fires when its situation arises: an app note built at request time (last item, never stored, same bytes for the same state), a tool's result (what is now in place and what is still unchecked), a tool's description (a rule about one tool), or the message itself (button sentences, `<workspace>`/`<print_issue>` blocks, the plate picture on file open). A sentence that restates what code enforces is deleted.
226	
227	**Why:** published practice (Anthropic skills' progressive disclosure, Replit decision-time guidance, Pydantic system reminders, Anthropic tools guide) and our own audit: rule lists fade and lose to the model's priors; four prompt sentences were an agent's precautions or restatements, never observed; the repeated-request line was Codex's own caution on 2026-10-12 and its test was derived from the sentence.
228	
229	**Form (Kenneth, 2026-10-17, revised later that day):** two kinds of skill, one loader, all `SKILL.md` on the page. An event skill has a `trigger` and the app injects it for the one request where the event happened; the model never chooses it. A discretionary skill has a `description` and the model may read it with the ported `skill_read` (consistent with Claude Code / Agent Skills; common skills may later be offered this way). Event skills never depend on the model choosing; the suspended skills branches (`feature/project-skills-routing`, 2d62184e37 README) failed on model routing and on content that repeated general knowledge, not on the container. Word-only situations get no skill until a transcript shows a gap.
230	
231	**Groups (Kenneth, 2026-10-17), one chip each, in order:** (1) a model is opened or imported (port the loader and skill_read, migrate the file-open text, fire on tool imports too; project_open by the model interrupts the turn, collects the load report with the existing collector and hands it to the new chat through the file-note path; the skill text adds the preset check and asks whether the AI should look at the model instead of attaching a picture); (2) slicing finished unsuccessfully (refusal reason into the project summary, event-driven slice wait); (3) other OrcaSlicer issues incl. the Explain/Fix canvas buttons; (4) project setup changed after a purpose was recorded. No skill for failed/not-run calls (JusPrin's own words). Prompt shrink is the last step. Tracker table in core-prompt-critique.md, "Skills by event".
232	
233	**How to apply:** when asked for a prompt rule, first ask which channel the situation belongs to; add a standing sentence only when a measured failure shows the model lacks the principle. The bridging sentence that makes state-delivered guidance work is "When a result or an app note names something unchecked, check it before moving on." The plan and disposition table live in the untracked `core-prompt-critique.md` ("Restructure plan", 2026-10-17), as a proposal: Kenneth wants plans presented and decided, not assumed. On 2026-10-17 he had my fast-forward merge of the state-guidance branch undone for that reason (reset, never revert: a revert would litter the log). Related: [[rule-lives-next-to-what-it-governs]], [[project-prompt-sections]], [[tool-call-approval-removed]].

331	A rule lives once, as close as possible to the thing it governs: a rule about one tool lives in that tool's description; a rule about the conversation (when to act, when to ask, record intent before preparing, reply language) lives in the prompt.

Applied in 2595f0556c, that stripped one-tool rules (skipped_confirmation settling, export slice check, project_open's message handling, intent_update's "do not infer") out of descriptions, which every caller sees — project, printer and filament chats and MCP clients — and left the other chats and MCP with nothing. The old reason for prompt-side policy, tool deferral hiding descriptions, is gone. Kenneth endorsed the correction on 2026-10-15.

Check the host's per-turn lines before calling them a rule's home: the "file-load reports are source data" developer line exists only for files the person opened, not for project_open called by the model or for MCP. Standing policy in instructions, facts in a tagged context block, …") with "I don't know why you talk this way. Really strange. Can you talk like a human?"

content.content:
## 2.3 Print intent

This surface answers: **What outcome does the user want?**

Instead of beginning with hundreds of process parameters, the product should ask for meaningful requirements.

### What should remain

- Intended use
- Visual versus functional priority
- Strength direction
- Accuracy requirements
- Important dimensions or clearances
- Heat, chemical, outdoor, food-contact, or flexibility requirements
- Desired surface quality
- Maximum acceptable print time
- Material or color requirements
- Acceptable and unacceptable support contact
- Whether this is a prototype or final part

### Why the agent cannot decide this alone

The same model can legitimately be printed with different orientations, materials, wall structures, infill, supports, and tolerances depending on its purpose.

A decorative prototype and a load-bearing final component may use identical geometry but require completely different plans.

### What the agent should do

Translate intent into technical settings. For example:

# Setup card and opening message: design options

2026-10-26. A design brainstorm for Kenneth, written from the reproduction in `card-headline-repro/` (jusprin-newui at 889d28681c) and from the code and design boards named below. No code was changed.

## What is wrong today, in plain words

The setup card is the box pinned at the top of the Agent pane. Its title is meant to be what the print is for, in the person's words, and its headline is the agent's one-line printing plan. Three things go wrong around it.

1. **The card says nothing about the print until the person states a purpose.** The agent may record a title and a plan only through one tool, `setup_record`, and that tool's description says to record only a purpose the person stated and to include one in every call (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`, "setup_record"). So before the person says what the print is for, the card's title is the process preset name ("0.20mm Standard @BBL A1") and there is no headline, even after the agent has confirmed the printer and both filaments (`opus-1-opened.jpg`, `opus-2-after-printer.jpg`). A chat where nobody ever states a purpose, like Kenneth's chat of 2026-10-21, stays like that for good.

2. **The card does not notice when the plate's contents change.** The purpose and plan belong to the chat and nothing updates them when a model is imported. The app does mark the plan as needing another look (`ProjectPersistence::on_edit` calls `mark_plan_needs_reassessment` for every edit that is not the agent's own, with the import's label as the reason), but that mark goes only to the model (`ProviderAgent.cpp`, `plan.validity`). The card is sent only the title and the headline (`card_context` in `Agent/AgentHost.cpp`), so after the bed-level sheet was imported it still read "Halloween headband costume for my kid · P1S PLA, sturdier walls…" with the state "Confirmed" (`sonnet-after-second-import.jpg`). "Confirmed" there comes from the estimate being recomputed, not from anyone confirming the plan.

3. **The event that started the chat is invisible, so the first message reads as if the agent spoke unprompted, about a moment the card no longer shows.** When a file opens, the host appends a note message holding the load report and starts the agent's turn from it (`AgentHost::on_file_loaded`). The page draws that note as nothing whenever the agent is set up (`bubble()` in `MessageList.tsx`). An import does get a visible row, "Import Object: <file> · you · 05:18", but only because OrcaSlicer records an undo step for it; the file that created the project leaves no row. The opening message then describes the moment of loading ("I opened the file, and it switched your setup… Which printer will you print this on?") directly under a card that already shows the printer chosen, the purpose stated and the plan made (`opus-3-top-after-purpose.jpg`, `sonnet-top-of-chat.jpg`).

A fourth, small one: the title is one line with an ellipsis (`.current-setup-title`), so a 60-character purpose ends in "sna…".

The design boards already point part of the way. The product definition asks for a "compact, editable intent summary" whose governing assumptions stay visible, and says the intent editor belongs at project creation and import (`agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md`, 2.3 and "Default Project-window composition"). The onboarding board "12 · Prepare intent" on the JusPrin v2 canvas draws that summary with an explicit empty state: "Intent · Not set · not submitted · Add a goal here or discuss it with the Agent". The card's own "Stress · No title" board, on the other hand, falls back to the preset name, which is what the code does. The design system has a Chat/System Line component, "a quiet one-line record of settings, plate tools, answered approvals, or background agent work", with a "you · 15:03" meta on the right.

## Question 1: the title and headline before a purpose is stated

**Option A, keep the preset name.** Status quo. It is honest about the presets but says nothing about the print, reads as a technical label, and the person has no idea the card is waiting for anything from them.

**Option B, the project's name, with a visible "purpose not set" line.** Every project is named after its file (`architecture.md`, "Opening and importing files"), and the name is already in the card's context as `projectName`. The title would read "find_my_hollow" or "petg-pla+support+interface", the presets line stays as it is, and where the headline will go there is one secondary line: "What is this print for? Tell the agent and it will plan around it." That line disappears the moment a purpose is recorded. The empty state is then the same thing the onboarding board draws, and the card never pretends to know the purpose. The cost is that a file name can be ugly, and the line is one more thing on a card the design wants compact.

**Option C, the file's own title when the 3MF carries one.** The load report has `details.title` from the 3MF ("Follow Me Arrow Headband – Festival headband"), which is the author's word for the object, not the model's guess and not a purpose. It reads far better than the file name. The cost is two sources for one slot: STL and STEP files have no title, so the card would say "Follow Me Arrow Headband" for one project and "AMS_disconnect_tool_raised_letters" for the next, and a 3MF title can be marketing copy.

**Recommendation: B, with C as a refinement if Kenneth wants it.** The project name is the one name the Plates and Project pane, Recent and the window already use, so the card agrees with the rest of the app. The headline slot stays empty until the agent records a plan (Question 2); the "purpose not set" line is what fills the gap, and it tells the person the one thing they can do that changes the card.

## Question 2: should recording a plan require a stated purpose?

**Option A, keep the requirement.** Purpose required and stated, or nothing is recorded. The rule exists because the two records drifted when they were separate tools (memory of 2026-10-20). The evidence from both runs is that it starves the card: after the printer and two filaments were confirmed, and a risky machine script found, the card still showed a preset name and no plan.

**Option B, make the purpose optional; keep "stated only".** The plan (headline, decisions, unverified, risks) can be recorded at any time; the purpose may be left out, and when it is, the one already recorded is kept. The rule that a purpose is never inferred stays exactly as written. The headline's rule gains one clause: it says how the print will be made, never what it is for. One tool still writes both records, so they cannot drift apart the way two tools let them. The risk is a weak model writing the inferred purpose into the headline anyway ("Festival headband in PLA…"); that is a prompt-eval case, not a reason to keep the card empty.

**Option C, allow a provisional purpose the agent infers from the file, marked as inferred.** The agent would record "Festival headband (from the file)" and the card would show it with that marker until the person states theirs. This is what a human assistant does out loud ("looks like a festival headband; is that what it's for?"), but it puts a guess in the slot Kenneth reserved for the person's words, and a person who never corrects it ends up with a plan built on a guess.

**Recommendation: B.** The purpose stays the person's. The plan is the agent's, and the agent has one whenever it has decided anything, which is usually well before the purpose is known (which printer, which of the file's two filaments, whether to keep the file's machine scripts). Record it, and the card shows the state of the agent's thinking from the second message on.

## Question 3: when the plate's contents change under a recorded purpose and plan

**Option A, show the app's own mark on the card and make the agent settle it.** The host already knows the plan needs another look and why ("Import Object: Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl"). Send `planValidity` and `planInvalidatedBy` to the card with the headline. The card then takes the pattern the "Setup card · Out of date" board already draws for estimates: the state label reads "Needs another look" instead of "Confirmed" or "Current", the headline is kept but drawn in the secondary text colour, and under the divider a warning row says "Plan made before: Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl was imported". The agent's reply after the import must then either record a new plan or restate the one that still holds, which clears the mark; the file-loaded skill gets that sentence. The purpose stays, because it is the person's statement and adding a part does not change what they said. The cost is a state the model can leave unsettled; the card then says so instead of saying "Confirmed", which is the point.

**Option B, clear the plan on every import.** The card falls back to the purpose with no headline and "No plan for the new contents yet". Simple and never stale, but it throws away a plan that often still holds (a 20 mm tool added beside the headband does not change the headband's strategy), and the same mark is set by every hand edit and every Undo, so the plan would vanish on a colour change.

**Option C, treat the purpose as stale too.** Mark the purpose when an object is added or removed and ask the person to restate it. Over-engineered: the purpose was about the headband and still is; the agent's job is to ask whether the new object is part of the same print, which Sonnet did in words.

**Recommendation: A.** The app is already right about the plan's state; the card should say what the app knows, and the agent should be the one to clear it. The state-label order becomes: working, then needs another look, then updated, then the existing states. "Confirmed" should never show while the plan carries the mark.

## Question 4: showing the event that started the chat

**Option A, draw the file-load note as a Chat/System Line.** The note already anchors the turn (`turnsOf` makes it the anchor and the agent's message its reply), it just draws as nothing. Draw it as the design system's system line: "Opened find_my_hollow.3mf as a new project · you · 05:16", or for an import "Added Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl · you · 05:20". The agent's message then reads as what it is, a dated reaction to that row, and the card above reads as now. An import already has a change row saying the same thing ("Import Object: … · you · 05:18"), so one of the two must go: keep the change row, which carries the revert affordance, and draw the note's line only when the load created the project. When the Agent could not speak, the note already draws as the "Notes about this file" card; that stays.

**Option B, a bubble in the person's voice ("I opened find_my_hollow.3mf").** Rejected: bubbles are words someone wrote, and the person wrote none.

**Option C, keep the note hidden and have the message name its trigger in words.** "You opened find_my_hollow.3mf, and it switched…". Cheapest, but it depends on the model every time, says nothing about when, and does nothing for the staleness under the card.

**Recommendation: A.** A dated row is also the honest answer to "the opening message goes stale": a message under "Opened … · 05:16" is visibly history once the card says something else, the same way the design's timeline treats an agent response as the answer to the turn above it. The reply choices under the opening message already close once answered, so the question does not stay clickable.

## Question 5: how long the opening message should be, and what it leaves to the card

Today's opening messages ran to about 230 words (Opus, four bullets and a question) and about 150 (Sonnet's import). Both repeated what the card shows (the preset switch, the two filaments) and the Opus one stated something wrong about the PLA that it had to correct in the next turn; length invites that. The skill already asks for "a few sentences".

**Option A, one decision and one question, under about 80 words.** Lead with the thing that decides whether or how the print can go ahead (which printer, a part that does not fit, a modified machine script), at most one secondary flag, then the one question. Presets, plate, estimates and object count are the card's and are not repeated. What was checked is the turn line's ("Worked for 9s · 3 actions", which opens into the list). The file author's advice waits until the gating decision is made, as the skill already says.

**Option B, the current shape.** Everything found, as bullets. It is the most-read message in the product and it sets the tone, but it goes stale fastest and overlaps the card most.

**Option C, a bare question when nothing blocks.** "Nothing needs attention. Which printer will you print this on?" and nothing else. Right for a clean STL on a known printer; too thin when the file switched the printer and carries two materials.

**Recommendation: A, with C as its lower bound.** The cap is a prompt-eval check (word count, bullet count, exactly one question), and the skill's "Write a short message" line becomes concrete numbers so it can be measured.

## Sketches

Panel at its narrow width. The card is on `surface.subtle`; rows under it are system lines in the secondary colour.

### A model file opened as a new project, before anyone has spoken

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Setup summary                      Not sliced │
```

# Setup card and opening message: design options

2026-10-26. A design brainstorm for Kenneth, written from the reproduction in `card-headline-repro/` (jusprin-newui at 889d28681c) and from the code and design boards named below. No code was changed.

## What is wrong today, in plain words

The setup card is the box pinned at the top of the Agent pane. Its title is meant to be what the print is for, in the person's words, and its headline is the agent's one-line printing plan. Three things go wrong around it.

1. **The card says nothing about the print until the person states a purpose.** The agent may record a title and a plan only through one tool, `setup_record`, and that tool's description says to record only a purpose the person stated and to include one in every call (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`, "setup_record"). So before the person says what the print is for, the card's title is the process preset name ("0.20mm Standard @BBL A1") and there is no headline, even after the agent has confirmed the printer and both filaments (`opus-1-opened.jpg`, `opus-2-after-printer.jpg`). A chat where nobody ever states a purpose, like Kenneth's chat of 2026-10-21, stays like that for good.

2. **The card does not notice when the plate's contents change.** The purpose and plan belong to the chat and nothing updates them when a model is imported. The app does mark the plan as needing another look (`ProjectPersistence::on_edit` calls `mark_plan_needs_reassessment` for every edit that is not the agent's own, with the import's label as the reason), but that mark goes only to the model (`ProviderAgent.cpp`, `plan.validity`). The card is sent only the title and the headline (`card_context` in `Agent/AgentHost.cpp`), so after the bed-level sheet was imported it still read "Halloween headband costume for my kid · P1S PLA, sturdier walls…" with the state "Confirmed" (`sonnet-after-second-import.jpg`). "Confirmed" there comes from the estimate being recomputed, not from anyone confirming the plan.

3. **The event that started the chat is invisible, so the first message reads as if the agent spoke unprompted, about a moment the card no longer shows.** When a file opens, the host appends a note message holding the load report and starts the agent's turn from it (`AgentHost::on_file_loaded`). The page draws that note as nothing whenever the agent is set up (`bubble()` in `MessageList.tsx`). An import does get a visible row, "Import Object: <file> · you · 05:18", but only because OrcaSlicer records an undo step for it; the file that created the project leaves no row. The opening message then describes the moment of loading ("I opened the file, and it switched your setup… Which printer will you print this on?") directly under a card that already shows the printer chosen, the purpose stated and the plan made (`opus-3-top-after-purpose.jpg`, `sonnet-top-of-chat.jpg`).

A fourth, small one: the title is one line with an ellipsis (`.current-setup-title`), so a 60-character purpose ends in "sna…".

The design boards already point part of the way. The product definition asks for a "compact, editable intent summary" whose governing assumptions stay visible, and says the intent editor belongs at project creation and import (`agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md`, 2.3 and "Default Project-window composition"). The onboarding board "12 · Prepare intent" on the JusPrin v2 canvas draws that summary with an explicit empty state: "Intent · Not set · not submitted · Add a goal here or discuss it with the Agent". The card's own "Stress · No title" board, on the other hand, falls back to the preset name, which is what the code does. The design system has a Chat/System Line component, "a quiet one-line record of settings, plate tools, answered approvals, or background agent work", with a "you · 15:03" meta on the right.

## Question 1: the title and headline before a purpose is stated

**Option A, keep the preset name.** Status quo. It is honest about the presets but says nothing about the print, reads as a technical label, and the person has no idea the card is waiting for anything from them.

**Option B, the project's name, with a visible "purpose not set" line.** Every project is named after its file (`architecture.md`, "Opening and importing files"), and the name is already in the card's context as `projectName`. The title would read "find_my_hollow" or "petg-pla+support+interface", the presets line stays as it is, and where the headline will go there is one secondary line: "What is this print for? Tell the agent and it will plan around it." That line disappears the moment a purpose is recorded. The empty state is then the same thing the onboarding board draws, and the card never pretends to know the purpose. The cost is that a file name can be ugly, and the line is one more thing on a card the design wants compact.

**Option C, the file's own title when the 3MF carries one.** The load report has `details.title` from the 3MF ("Follow Me Arrow Headband – Festival headband"), which is the author's word for the object, not the model's guess and not a purpose. It reads far better than the file name. The cost is two sources for one slot: STL and STEP files have no title, so the card would say "Follow Me Arrow Headband" for one project and "AMS_disconnect_tool_raised_letters" for the next, and a 3MF title can be marketing copy.

**Recommendation: B, with C as a refinement if Kenneth wants it.** The project name is the one name the Plates and Project pane, Recent and the window already use, so the card agrees with the rest of the app. The headline slot stays empty until the agent records a plan (Question 2); the "purpose not set" line is what fills the gap, and it tells the person the one thing they can do that changes the card.

## Question 2: should recording a plan require a stated purpose?

**Option A, keep the requirement.** Purpose required and stated, or nothing is recorded. The rule exists because the two records drifted when they were separate tools (memory of 2026-10-20). The evidence from both runs is that it starves the card: after the printer and two filaments were confirmed, and a risky machine script found, the card still showed a preset name and no plan.

**Option B, make the purpose optional; keep "stated only".** The plan (headline, decisions, unverified, risks) can be recorded at any time; the purpose may be left out, and when it is, the one already recorded is kept. The rule that a purpose is never inferred stays exactly as written. The headline's rule gains one clause: it says how the print will be made, never what it is for. One tool still writes both records, so they cannot drift apart the way two tools let them. The risk is a weak model writing the inferred purpose into the headline anyway ("Festival headband in PLA…"); that is a prompt-eval case, not a reason to keep the card empty.

**Option C, allow a provisional purpose the agent infers from the file, marked as inferred.** The agent would record "Festival headband (from the file)" and the card would show it with that marker until the person states theirs. This is what a human assistant does out loud ("looks like a festival headband; is that what it's for?"), but it puts a guess in the slot Kenneth reserved for the person's words, and a person who never corrects it ends up with a plan built on a guess.

**Recommendation: B.** The purpose stays the person's. The plan is the agent's, and the agent has one whenever it has decided anything, which is usually well before the purpose is known (which printer, which of the file's two filaments, whether to keep the file's machine scripts). Record it, and the card shows the state of the agent's thinking from the second message on.

## Question 3: when the plate's contents change under a recorded purpose and plan

**Option A, show the app's own mark on the card and make the agent settle it.** The host already knows the plan needs another look and why ("Import Object: Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl"). Send `planValidity` and `planInvalidatedBy` to the card with the headline. The card then takes the pattern the "Setup card · Out of date" board already draws for estimates: the state label reads "Needs another look" instead of "Confirmed" or "Current", the headline is kept but drawn in the secondary text colour, and under the divider a warning row says "Plan made before: Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl was imported". The agent's reply after the import must then either record a new plan or restate the one that still holds, which clears the mark; the file-loaded skill gets that sentence. The purpose stays, because it is the person's statement and adding a part does not change what they said. The cost is a state the model can leave unsettled; the card then says so instead of saying "Confirmed", which is the point.

**Option B, clear the plan on every import.** The card falls back to the purpose with no headline and "No plan for the new contents yet". Simple and never stale, but it throws away a plan that often still holds (a 20 mm tool added beside the headband does not change the headband's strategy), and the same mark is set by every hand edit and every Undo, so the plan would vanish on a colour change.

**Option C, treat the purpose as stale too.** Mark the purpose when an object is added or removed and ask the person to restate it. Over-engineered: the purpose was about the headband and still is; the agent's job is to ask whether the new object is part of the same print, which Sonnet did in words.

**Recommendation: A.** The app is already right about the plan's state; the card should say what the app knows, and the agent should be the one to clear it. The state-label order becomes: working, then needs another look, then updated, then the existing states. "Confirmed" should never show while the plan carries the mark.

## Question 4: showing the event that started the chat

**Option A, draw the file-load note as a Chat/System Line.** The note already anchors the turn (`turnsOf` makes it the anchor and the agent's message its reply), it just draws as nothing. Draw it as the design system's system line: "Opened find_my_hollow.3mf as a new project · you · 05:16", or for an import "Added Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl · you · 05:20". The agent's message then reads as what it is, a dated reaction to that row, and the card above reads as now. An import already has a change row saying the same thing ("Import Object: … · you · 05:18"), so one of the two must go: keep the change row, which carries the revert affordance, and draw the note's line only when the load created the project. When the Agent could not speak, the note already draws as the "Notes about this file" card; that stays.

**Option B, a bubble in the person's voice ("I opened find_my_hollow.3mf").** Rejected: bubbles are words someone wrote, and the person wrote none.

**Option C, keep the note hidden and have the message name its trigger in words.** "You opened find_my_hollow.3mf, and it switched…". Cheapest, but it depends on the model every time, says nothing about when, and does nothing for the staleness under the card.

**Recommendation: A.** A dated row is also the honest answer to "the opening message goes stale": a message under "Opened … · 05:16" is visibly history once the card says something else, the same way the design's timeline treats an agent response as the answer to the turn above it. The reply choices under the opening message already close once answered, so the question does not stay clickable.

## Question 5: how long the opening message should be, and what it leaves to the card

Today's opening messages ran to about 230 words (Opus, four bullets and a question) and about 150 (Sonnet's import). Both repeated what the card shows (the preset switch, the two filaments) and the Opus one stated something wrong about the PLA that it had to correct in the next turn; length invites that. The skill already asks for "a few sentences".

**Option A, one decision and one question, under about 80 words.** Lead with the thing that decides whether or how the print can go ahead (which printer, a part that does not fit, a modified machine script), at most one secondary flag, then the one question. Presets, plate, estimates and object count are the card's and are not repeated. What was checked is the turn line's ("Worked for 9s · 3 actions", which opens into the list). The file author's advice waits until the gating decision is made, as the skill already says.

**Option B, the current shape.** Everything found, as bullets. It is the most-read message in the product and it sets the tone, but it goes stale fastest and overlaps the card most.

**Option C, a bare question when nothing blocks.** "Nothing needs attention. Which printer will you print this on?" and nothing else. Right for a clean STL on a known printer; too thin when the file switched the printer and carries two materials.

**Recommendation: A, with C as its lower bound.** The cap is a prompt-eval check (word count, bullet count, exactly one question), and the skill's "Write a short message" line becomes concrete numbers so it can be measured.

The cost is a state the model can leave unsettled; the card then says so instead of saying "Confirmed", which is the point.

**Option B, clear the plan on every import.** The card falls back to the purpose with no headline and "No plan for the new contents yet". Simple and never stale, but it throws away a plan that often still holds (a 20 mm tool added beside the headband does not change the headband's strategy), and the same mark is set by every hand edit and every Undo, so the plan would vanish on a colour change.

**Option C, treat the purpose as stale too.** Mark the purpose when an object is added or removed and ask the person to restate it. Over-engineered: the purpose was about the headband and still is; the agent's job is to ask whether the new object is part of the same print, which Sonnet did in words.

**Recommendation: A.** The app is already right about the plan's state; the card should say what the app knows, and the agent should be the one to clear it. The state-label order becomes: working, then needs another look, then updated, then the existing states. "Confirmed" should never show while the plan carries the mark.

## Question 4: showing the event that started the chat

**Option A, draw the file-load note as a Chat/System Line.** The note already anchors the turn (`turnsOf` makes it the anchor and the agent's message its reply), it just draws as nothing. Draw it as the design system's system line: "Opened find_my_hollow.3mf as a new project · you · 05:16", or for an import "Added Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl · you · 05:20". The agent's message then reads as what it is, a dated reaction to that row, and the card above reads as now. An import already has a change row saying the same thing ("Import Object: … · you · 05:18"), so one of the two must go: keep the change row, which carries the revert affordance, and draw the note's line only when the load created the project. When the Agent could not speak, the note already draws as the "Notes about this file" card; that stays.

**Option B, a bubble in the person's voice ("I opened find_my_hollow.3mf").** Rejected: bubbles are words someone wrote, and the person wrote none.

**Option C, keep the note hidden and have the message name its trigger in words.** "You opened find_my_hollow.3mf, and it switched…". Cheapest, but it depends on the model every time, says nothing about when, and does nothing for the staleness under the card.

**Recommendation: A.** A dated row is also the honest answer to "the opening message goes stale": a message under "Opened … · 05:16" is visibly history once the card says something else, the same way the design's timeline treats an agent response as the answer to the turn above it. The reply choices under the opening message already close once answered, so the question does not stay clickable.

## Question 5: how long the opening message should be, and what it leaves to the card

Today's opening messages ran to about 230 words (Opus, four bullets and a question) and about 150 (Sonnet's import). Both repeated what the card shows (the preset switch, the two filaments) and the Opus one stated something wrong about the PLA that it had to correct in the next turn; length invites that. The skill already asks for "a few sentences".

**Option A, one decision and one question, under about 80 words.** Lead with the thing that decides whether or how the print can go ahead (which printer, a part that does not fit, a modified machine script), at most one secondary flag, then the one question. Presets, plate, estimates and object count are the card's and are not repeated. What was checked is the turn line's ("Worked for 9s · 3 actions", which opens into the list). The file author's advice waits until the gating decision is made, as the skill already says.

**Option B, the current shape.** Everything found, as bullets. It is the most-read message in the product and it sets the tone, but it goes stale fastest and overlaps the card most.

**Option C, a bare question when nothing blocks.** "Nothing needs attention. Which printer will you print this on?" and nothing else. Right for a clean STL on a known printer; too thin when the file switched the printer and carries two materials.

**Recommendation: A, with C as its lower bound.** The cap is a prompt-eval check (word count, bullet count, exactly one question), and the skill's "Write a short message" line becomes concrete numbers so it can be measured.

## What this does not settle

- The slice that sat at 80% during the Sonnet run is out of scope here, as the task said.
- Whether a plan recorded before a purpose should count as "checked against the purpose" once one is stated. Today a first or changed purpose fires the setup-changed skill, which asks the agent to check the presets; that should keep working unchanged, and a plan recorded earlier would simply be re-recorded then.
- The one-line title. The design's "Stress · Long title" board also clips it with an ellipsis, so the clipping is as designed; whether a 60-character limit and a one-line title can both stay is a small decision below.

## Decisions that are Kenneth's

Each of these changes what the person sees, so none is mine to make.

1. **Before a purpose is stated, should the card's title be the project's name, with a "what is this print for" line under the presets, instead of the process preset name?** Yes gives the person a card about their project and a visible invitation to state the purpose; no keeps the preset name and the blank. I recommend yes. A sub-question: should a 3MF's own title replace the file name when the file carries one? I lean no, for consistency with the rest of the app, but it reads better.

2. **May the agent record a plan before the person has stated a purpose, with the purpose still never inferred?** Yes puts the agent's plan on the card from its second message; no keeps the card empty for every chat that starts from a file until the person volunteers a purpose. I recommend yes.

3. **When the plate's contents change under a recorded plan, should the card show the app's "needs another look" mark and the reason, keep the headline in a quieter colour, and never say "Confirmed" until the agent settles it?** The alternative is to clear the plan outright on every such change. I recommend showing the mark, because it is already correct and because clearing would also fire on every hand edit and Undo.

4. **Should the file that created the project get a dated system line in the chat ("Opened X as a new project · you · 12:31"), with imports keeping their existing change row?** The alternative is to leave the event invisible and ask the model to name it in words. I recommend the row.

5. **Should the opening message be capped at about 80 words, at most two bullets and one question, leaving presets, plate and estimates to the card and the checks to the turn line?** The alternative is today's bullet list of everything found. I recommend the cap, measured by the prompt evals.

6. **Should the title wrap to two lines before clipping, or should the purpose limit drop from 60 characters to what one line holds (about 45 at the narrow width)?** Either removes "sna…". I lean towards two lines, since the person's words are the one thing on the card that should not be cut.

The card's title and plan come only from the setup_record tool, whose description requires a purpose the person stated in every call, so a chat that starts from a file shows a preset name and no plan until someone volunteers a purpose. # Setup card and opening message: design options

2026-10-26, revised the same day after Kenneth's feedback: start from why the card exists, and prefer the shape that is too simple to have problems over the one with no obvious problems. Written from the reproduction in `card-headline-repro/` (jusprin-newui at 889d28681c) and the code and design boards listed at the end. No code was changed.

## Why the card exists

The person is talking to an agent that changes their project. The project's real state lives in OrcaSlicer, not in any message, and messages go stale the moment the next turn happens. The chat is a log; the All settings panel is an editor; the card is the one place in the Agent pane that is always *now*. It answers, without scrolling and without reading: what is this print being made with right now, what is the agent working toward, and what will it cost. The product definition asks for exactly that set on the default window: a compact printer pointer, a compact editable intent summary, a compact pinned agent plan, and the highest unresolved risk (`agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md`, "Default Project-window composition" and 2.3 "Print intent").

Two things follow from that purpose, and they decide every question below.

First, **everything on the card must be something the app can know is true now.** Presets, plate, estimates and object counts come from OrcaSlicer and are true by construction. The purpose and the plan are text the agent wrote, and the card can only show them honestly if the app tracks whether the project has moved on since they were written. For the plan it already does (`mark_plan_needs_reassessment` on every edit that is not the agent's own). For the purpose it does not need to: those are the person's words and change only when the person changes them.

Second, **anything that is a record of a moment belongs in the timeline, not on the card.** "Updated" for one minute after the agent's change, the last project step with its Undo, the estimate before and after, "You set Wall loops 3 outside the agent. Your current settings are preserved.", "Confirmed": these are all notes about something that just happened. The timeline already draws every change as a row with who and when and a revert point (`ChangeRows.tsx`). The card drawing them too is why it has twelve named states today (`setupPresentation` in `SetupCard.tsx`: Preset fallback, No agent, Agent working, Updated, Confirmed, Edited by you, Out of date, Not sliced, Current, Earlier setup, Saved sliced snapshot, Sliced & sent), and why each fix for one of them has opened a hole for the next.

## What is wrong today, in plain words

1. **The card says nothing about the print until the person states a purpose.** The one tool that writes the card's title and plan, `setup_record`, requires a stated purpose in every call (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`). So after a file opens, the title is the process preset name and there is no headline, even once the agent has confirmed the printer and both filaments (`opus-1-opened.jpg`, `opus-2-after-printer.jpg`). A chat where nobody states a purpose, like Kenneth's of 2026-10-21, stays that way.

2. **The card does not notice when the plate's contents change.** The app marks the plan as needing another look after an import, with the import's label as the reason, but sends the mark only to the model (`ProviderAgent.cpp`); the card gets the title and headline alone (`card_context` in `AgentHost.cpp`). So after the bed-level sheet was imported the card still read the headband plan and said "Confirmed" (`sonnet-after-second-import.jpg`). "Confirmed" there came from the estimate being recomputed, not from anyone confirming anything.

3. **The event that started the chat is invisible, so the opening message reads as unprompted, about a moment the card no longer shows.** The host appends a note holding the load report and starts the agent's turn from it (`AgentHost::on_file_loaded`); the page draws that note as nothing when the agent is set up (`bubble()` in `MessageList.tsx`). An import gets a visible row only because OrcaSlicer records an undo step for it; the file that created the project leaves none. The message then describes the moment of loading under a card that shows a later state (`opus-3-top-after-purpose.jpg`, `sonnet-top-of-chat.jpg`).

And a small one: the title is one line with an ellipsis, so a 60-character purpose ends in "sna…".

## The simple card

Six slots, each with one source and one empty form. No state machine; the only thing on the right of the eyebrow is "Agent working" while a turn runs, because that is the one card-wide "now" fact.

```
Setup summary                        [Agent working]
<purpose the person stated · else the project's name>
<process · first filament (+n)>
<plan headline · else nothing>
  ↳ when the app has marked the plan: "Plan needs another look · <reason>"
<estimates · "Not sliced yet" · "Recomputing…" · "Previous estimates · not current">
<warning rows from the app's own checks, e.g. printer reports PLA, setup uses PETG>
All settings
```

The rule for the two agent-written slots is the same rule the estimates slot already has: a record the app knows is behind the project is shown with "not current" beside it, never silently kept and never silently deleted. The estimates do this today ("Previous estimates · not current" on the "Setup card · Out of date" board); the plan gets the identical treatment.

What leaves the card, and where it already lives:

| Leaves the card | Already lives in |
|---|---|
| "Updated" for a minute, the last step, Undo, estimate before → after | the change rows under the turn, with "Revert to here" |
| "Edited by you outside the agent" note | the person's change row, plus "Plan needs another look · Wall loops 2 → 3" on the card |
| "Confirmed" | nothing; it was the recompute state wearing the wrong word |
| The separate "Preset fallback" and "No agent" renderings | the same six slots; with no agent the plan slot reads "No agent configured" |

The saved card of an earlier chat (historical, "Saved with this chat") is a different object, a snapshot, and is not changed by this note.

The cost of the cut is one click: Undo of the agent's last project step was on the card; it becomes the timeline row's revert, which is one scroll away at most because the row sits under the turn that made it. I think that is the right trade; the card should not carry an action whose meaning changes a minute later.

## The five questions under that shape

**1. Title and headline before a purpose is stated.** The title slot shows the purpose or, when there is none, the project's name, which is the file's name (`architecture.md`, "Opening and importing files") and is already in the card's context as `projectName`. Nothing else: no "purpose not set" hint line, no preset name. Asking for the purpose is the agent's job in its message, where it already is. The headline slot is empty until the agent records a plan.

The earlier draft of this note proposed a hint line and, as a refinement, the 3MF's own title. Both are extra states for the no-purpose case; the project name is one rule that is true in every case and matches how the Plates and Project pane and Recent name the same thing.

**2. Should recording a plan require a stated purpose?** No. The purpose becomes optional in `setup_record`; when it is left out, the recorded one is kept. The rule that a purpose is never inferred stays as written, and the headline's rule gains one clause: it says how the print will be made, never what it is for. This removes a coupling rather than adding anything. Both records still come through one tool, so they cannot drift apart the way the two old tools let them. The evidence for the change is both runs: the agent had chosen a printer and two filaments and found a risky machine script, and the card showed none of it.

**3. When the plate's contents change under a recorded purpose and plan.** Send the plan's validity and reason to the card beside the headline. The headline line reads "Plan needs another look · imported Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl" until the agent either records a new plan or restates the one that holds, both of which clear the mark; the file-loaded skill tells it to do one or the other in the same reply. The purpose is untouched: adding a part does not change what the person said the print is for. Nothing is cleared automatically, because the same mark is set by every hand edit and every Undo, and a plan that vanished on a colour change would be a worse surprise than one that says it needs a look.

**4. Showing the event that started the chat.** Every event that starts a turn gets a row; the hidden note is the one exception today and it goes. The file-load note already anchors the turn (`turnsOf`); draw it as the design system's Chat/System Line, "Opened find_my_hollow.3mf as a new project · you · 12:16", when the load created the project. An import already has its change row ("Import Object: … · you · 05:18"), which carries the revert point, so the note draws nothing there and the change row stays the trigger. The agent's message is then a dated reply to a dated row, and the card above is now. That is the whole answer to "the opening message goes stale": it is history, drawn as history, like every other turn in the design's timeline. The reply choices under it already close once answered.

**5. How long the opening message should be.** About 80 words, at most two bullets, exactly one question, measured by the prompt evals. It leads with the decision that gates printing (which printer, a part that does not fit, a modified machine script), and leaves presets, plate and estimates to the card and the list of checks to the turn line ("Worked for 9s · 3 actions"). Today's messages ran to about 230 words (Opus) and 150 (Sonnet), repeated the card, and the long one stated something wrong that the next turn had to correct.

## Sketches

Panel at its narrow width. The card is on `surface.subtle`; the rows under it are system lines in the secondary colour.

### A model file opened as a new project, before anyone has spoken

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Setup summary                                 │
│ petg-pla+support+interface                    │   ← project name; no purpose yet
│ 0.20mm Standard · Generic PETG +1             │
│ Not sliced yet                                │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ All settings                                  │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Opened petg-pla+support+interface.3mf as a    │   ← Chat/System Line
│ new project                        you · 12:31│
│                                               │
│ This file was made for the Bambu Lab A1 and   │   ← ≤ 80 words, one question
│ switched your printer to it. The headband is  │
│ 254 × 252 mm, so of your printers only the A1 │
│ and the Qidi X-Plus 4 can hold it. It also    │
│ uses PETG with a PLA separating layer, which  │
│ needs a filament changer. Which printer will  │
│ you print this on?                            │
│ (Bambu Lab A1) (Qidi X-Plus 4) (Anycubic K…)  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### The same chat after the printer was chosen, still no purpose

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Setup summary                                 │
│ petg-pla+support+interface                    │
│ 0.20mm Standard · Generic PETG +1             │
│ A1 confirmed, file's PETG + PLA kept, machine │   ← plan recorded without a purpose
│ scripts to review                             │
│ Not sliced yet                                │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ All settings                                  │
```

When the person says "it's part of my kid's Halloween costume", the title becomes their words and nothing else on the card or in the chat moves.

### A model imported into a project that already has a purpose and a plan

```
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Setup summary                                 │
│ Halloween headband costume for my kid         │   ← the person's words stay
│ 0.20mm Standard · Bambu PLA Basic +2          │
│ Plan needs another look ·                     │   ← the app's mark, same rule as estimates
│ imported Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl             │
│ ◷ ~52 min  ⬡ 31 g  ▦ Plate 1                  │
│ ──────────────────────────────────────────── │
│ All settings                                  │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ✎ Import Object: Print_Bed_Level_Test.stl     │   ← the existing change row is the trigger
│                                    you · 05:20│
│                                               │
│ That sheet is a 203 × 203 mm bed-levelling    │
│ test, one layer thick, not part of the        │
│ headband, and it cannot share plate 1 with    │
│ the arrow. Should I put it on its own plate,  │
│ or leave it out of this print?                │
│ (Own plate) (Leave it out)                    │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The agent's reply re-records or confirms the plan, and the headline line returns.

## The alternative I considered and set aside

Drop the purpose and plan from the card altogether and show only OrcaSlicer facts: project name, presets, estimates, warnings, All settings. That card can never be wrong, and it needs no staleness rule at all. I set it aside because it would no longer answer "what is the agent working toward", which is half of why the card exists, and because the product definition puts the intent summary and the pinned plan on the default window. If Kenneth would rather have the card that cannot lie than the card that says when it might, this is the shape, and it is simpler still.

## What this does not settle

- The slice that sat at 80% during the Sonnet run, out of scope as the task said.
- Whether a plan recorded before a purpose counts as checked once a purpose is stated. Today a first or changed purpose fires the setup-changed skill, which asks the agent to check the presets; that keeps working, and the agent re-records then.

## Decisions that are Kenneth's

Each changes what the person sees, so none is mine. Each is a question with its alternative and my lean.

1. **Should the card be cut to the six slots above, with the moment-of-change notes (Updated, last step with Undo, estimate delta, edited-by-you) left to the timeline rows?** The alternative keeps today's card and fixes the three faults inside it. I recommend the cut; it is the change that makes the other five small.

2. **Before a purpose is stated, should the title be the project's name, with no hint line?** The alternatives are the preset name (today) or a hint line inviting the purpose. I recommend the project name alone.

3. **May the agent record a plan before the person has stated a purpose, with the purpose still never inferred?** No keeps the card empty for every chat that starts from a file. I recommend yes.

4. **When the project changes under a plan, should the headline line read "Plan needs another look · reason" until the agent re-records or confirms, with the purpose untouched and nothing cleared automatically?** The alternative is to clear the plan on such changes. I recommend the line.

5. **Should the file that created the project get a dated system line in the chat, with imports keeping their change row?** The alternative is to leave the event invisible and ask the model to name it in words. I recommend the row.

6. **Should the opening message be capped at about 80 words, two bullets and one question?** The alternative is today's bullet list of everything found. I recommend the cap.

7. **Should the title wrap to two lines, or should the purpose limit drop to what one line holds (about 45 characters at the narrow width)?** Either removes "sna…". I lean towards two lines, since the person's words are the one thing on the card that should not be cut.

8. **Or, instead of 1 to 4: should the card show only OrcaSlicer facts and no agent-written text at all?** Simplest of all and never wrong; it gives up the pinned purpose and plan. I lean against, for the reason above, but it is the honest other end of the simplicity scale.

## Sources read

- `card-headline-repro/REPORT.md`, its five screenshots and both saved chats (`repro-project*/current-state.json`).
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/components/SetupCard.tsx` (`setupPresentation`, `presetsLine`), `MessageList.tsx` (`bubble`, `turnsOf`), `ChangeRows.tsx`, `FileNotesCard.tsx`, `skills/file-loaded/SKILL.md`, `skills/project-setup-changed/SKILL.md`.
- `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/AgentHost.cpp` (`card_context`, `on_file_loaded`, `continue_after_tool`, the chat-title generator), `ToolRegistry.cpp` (`setup_record`), `ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp` (the `SetupRecord` handler), `ProjectPersistence.cpp` and `ProjectStateDocument.cpp` (`mark_plan_needs_reassessment`), `ProviderAgent.cpp`.
- `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `design-system.md`, `architecture.md` ("Opening and importing files"), `product-definition.md` (2.3 "Print intent", "Default Project-window composition").
- The JusPrin v2 canvas: boards "Setup card · Current · Collapsed/Expanded", "Setup card · Out of date", "Stress · No title", "Stress · Long title", "Pinned Setup Card", "Chat/System Line · Light & Dark", "print-timeline-panel-full", "12 · Prepare intent", "message-states · conversation content matrix". The Setup Card Review artifact of 2026-10-09.

# Setup card and opening message: design options

2026-10-26, revised the same day after Kenneth's feedback: start from why the card exists, and prefer the shape that is too simple to have problems over the one with no obvious problems. Written from the reproduction in `card-headline-repro/` (jusprin-newui at 889d28681c) and the code and design boards listed at the end. No code was changed.

## Why the card exists

The person is talking to an agent that changes their project. The project's real state lives in OrcaSlicer, not in any message, and messages go stale the moment the next turn happens. The chat is a log; the All settings panel is an editor; the card is the one place in the Agent pane that is always *now*. It answers, without scrolling and without reading: what is this print being made with right now, what is the agent working toward, and what will it cost. The product definition asks for exactly that set on the default window: a compact printer pointer, a compact editable intent summary, a compact pinned agent plan, and the highest unresolved risk (`agent-docs/jusprin/product-definition.md`, "Default Project-window composition" and 2.3 "Print intent").

Two things follow from that purpose, and they decide every question below.

First, **everything on the card must be something the app can know is true now.** Presets, plate, estimates and object counts come from OrcaSlicer and are true by construction. The purpose and the plan are text the agent wrote, and the card can only show them honestly if the app tracks whether the project has moved on since they were written. For the plan it already does (`mark_plan_needs_reassessment` on every edit that is not the agent's own). For the purpose it does not need to: those are the person's words and change only when the person changes them.

Second, **anything that is a record of a moment belongs in the timeline, not on the card.** "Updated" for one minute after the agent's change, the last project step with its Undo, the estimate before and after, "You set Wall loops 3 outside the agent. Your current settings are preserved.", "Confirmed": these are all notes about something that just happened. The timeline already draws every change as a row with who and when and a revert point (`ChangeRows.tsx`). The card drawing them too is why it has twelve named states today (`setupPresentation` in `SetupCard.tsx`: Preset fallback, No agent, Agent working, Updated, Confirmed, Edited by you, Out of date, Not sliced, Current, Earlier setup, Saved sliced snapshot, Sliced & sent), and why each fix for one of them has opened a hole for the next.

## What is wrong today, in plain words

1. **The card says nothing about the print until the person states a purpose.** The one tool that writes the card's title and plan, `setup_record`, requires a stated purpose in every call (`Agent/ToolRegistry.cpp`). So after a file opens, the title is the process preset name and there is no headline, even once the agent has confirmed the printer and both filaments (`opus-1-opened.jpg`, `opus-2-after-printer.jpg`). A chat where nobody states a purpose, like Kenneth's of 2026-10-21, stays that way.

2. **The card does not notice when the plate's contents change.** The app marks the plan as needing another look after an import, with the import's label as the reason, but sends the mark only to the model (`ProviderAgent.cpp`); the card gets the title and headline alone (`card_context` in `AgentHost.cpp`). So after the bed-level sheet was imported the card still read the headband plan and said "Confirmed" (`sonnet-after-second-import.jpg`). "Confirmed" there came from the estimate being recomputed, not from anyone confirming anything.

3. **The event that started the chat is invisible, so the opening message reads as unprompted, about a moment the card no longer shows.** The host appends a note holding the load report and starts the agent's turn from it (`AgentHost::on_file_loaded`); the page draws that note as nothing when the agent is set up (`bubble()` in `MessageList.tsx`). An import gets a visible row only because OrcaSlicer records an undo step for it; the file that created the project leaves none. The message then describes the moment of loading under a card that shows a later state (`opus-3-top-after-purpose.jpg`, `sonnet-top-of-chat.jpg`).

And a small one: the title is one line with an ellipsis, so a 60-character purpose ends in "sna…".

## The simple card

Six slots, each with one source and one empty form. No state machine; the only thing on the right of the eyebrow is "Agent working" while a turn runs, because that is the one card-wide "now" fact.

```
Setup summary                        [Agent working]
<purpose the person stated · else the project's name>
<process · first filament (+n)>
<plan headline · else nothing>
  ↳ when the app has marked the plan: "Plan needs another look · <reason>"
<estimates · "Not sliced yet" · "Recomputing…" · "Previous estimates · not current">
<warning rows from the app's own checks, e.g. printer reports PLA, setup uses PETG>
All settings
```

The rule for the two agent-written slots is the same rule the estimates slot already has: a record the app knows is behind the project is shown with "not current" beside it, never silently kept and never silently deleted. The estimates do this today ("Previous estimates · not current" on the "Setup card · Out of date" board); the plan gets the identical treatment.

What leaves the card, and where it already lives:

| Leaves the card | Already lives in |
|---|---|
| "Updated" for a minute, the last step, Undo, estimate before → after | the change rows under the turn, with "Revert to here" |
| "Edited by you outside the agent" note | the person's change row, plus "Plan needs another look · Wall loops 2 → 3" on the card |
| "Confirmed" | nothing; it was the recompute state wearing the wrong word |
| The separate "Preset fallback" and "No agent" renderings | the same six slots; with no agent the plan slot reads "No agent configured" |

The saved card of an earlier chat (historical, "Saved with this chat") is a different object, a snapshot, and is not changed by this note.

The cost of the cut is one click: Undo of the agent's last project step was on the card; it becomes the timeline row's revert, which is one scroll away at most because the row sits under the turn that made it. Title and headline before a purpose is stated.** The title slot shows the purpose or, when there is none, the project's name, which is the file's name (`architecture.md`, "Opening and importing files") and is already in the card's context as `projectName`. Nothing else: no "purpose not set" hint line, no preset name. Asking for the purpose is the agent's job in its message, where it already is.
